set.body: These modules call cliWrappers.ts's callLLM directly, which uses Bun.spawn -- only callable from a real Bun process, never from browser-executed React code (Bun is undefined in the browser; confirmed via typeof Bun === 'undefined' in a live browser test). DiagramGenExtension.tsx hit this exact bug during epic C story 1 and was fixed by routing through src/lib/llmClient.ts (Tauri run_llm_cli command, or the dev server's POST /api/llm) instead of calling cliWrappers.callLLM directly. set.body: DOMPurify's svg-only sanitize profile in src/lib/sanitize.ts hard-excludes the foreignObject tag (a known SVG XSS vector), which is how Mermaid renders flowchart/state-diagram node labels (HTML span/p inside foreignObject, not plain SVG <text>). Result: node shapes render but all label text is silently stripped. Fixed by adding the html DOMPurify profile, ADD_TAGS:['foreignobject'], and HTML_INTEGRATION_POINTS:{foreignobject:true} (DOMPurify enforces HTML-in-SVG namespace rules independently of the tag allowlist). Verified live: flowchart labels (Start/Is it working?/Yes/No/Great!/Debug) now render correctly.
set.title: sanitizeSvg strips Mermaid's HTML-based node labels (foreignObject), leaving diagrams with empty shapes and no text

set.body: Observed while live-verifying the sanitizeSvg fix: when an AI-generated diagram has invalid Mermaid syntax, DiagramGenExtension.tsx correctly catches the error and shows its own inline message, but mermaid.render() itself also has a side effect of appending a bomb-icon error overlay to document.body -- outside any of our React-managed containers, appearing as a stray fixed-position toast unrelated to the failing block's on-screen position. Cosmetic, not a data-loss or security issue; low priority. Would need to intercept/suppress mermaid's own DOM-injecting error path (e.g. via its internal error renderer config) or remove the stray node after each render attempt.
set.title: Mermaid's internal parse-error UI ('bomb' error graphic) injects into document.body instead of staying inside the failing block's container

set.body: Decision (user-confirmed): use the locally-installed `imagen` CLI (wraps Google's Gemini Imagen API, already configured with a working API key on this machine). Images are stored as base64 data URIs directly on the node's src attribute (ponytail: mirrors how DiagramGenExtension stores rendered content inline; avoids needing workspace-relative file paths / Tauri asset-protocol plumbing for v1 -- upgrade path is real file storage if doc-size bloat becomes a problem). Verified end-to-end live in-browser with a real (non-mocked) imagen call producing a real 1408px PNG.

set.body: Found by the first console baseline measurement in Phase 0. The welcome document serializes an unset diagram as 'content: null'. Three extensions each carried their own copy of the key:value parser, and all three turned that into the 4-character string "null" -- truthy, so DiagramGenExtension's render guard let it through and mermaid threw UnknownDiagramError on every page load. Fixed by extracting one shared parser (blockAttrs.ts) treating serialized null/undefined as unset, and pointing Dataset/ImageGen/DiagramGen at it. ImageGen had the same latent defect via 'src: null'.

set.body: Found while proving the E2E network gate actually bites. server.ts fell through to the SPA shell for ANY unmatched path, so fetch() for a missing note returned HTTP 200 carrying a page of HTML. WebStorage.readFile checks res.ok, so it treated that as a successful read and handed the editor HTML source as the note's markdown -- worse than the 'error loading file' behaviour B2 was thought to have. It also made missing files structurally invisible to the network gate. Fixed: unknown /api/* returns 404 JSON, a missing path whose last segment has a file extension returns 404, and only extensionless routes fall through to the SPA shell. /favicon.ico now answers 204 so the browser's unprompted request is not gate noise.

set.body: Bun.serve defaults to hostname 0.0.0.0 when none is given, so the dev server listened on every interface. It already exposed /api/llm and /api/image, which spawn local subprocesses, and Phase 1 added /api/fs/write on top -- so anything on the same network could write files inside the workspace and run CLI tools, with no authentication. The workspace jail constrains where a write lands; it says nothing about who may ask. Now binds 127.0.0.1, overridable via MOTION_HOST. Also removed the Google Fonts entries still sitting in the Tauri CSP after the font links were dropped -- permissions granted for something the app no longer does. Surfaced by the design-doc generation pass reading the code end to end.

set.body: Opening a saved document with custom block node views logged 'flushSync was called from inside a lifecycle method' at console.error level, three times per load. Tiptap dispatches transactions synchronously, so setting React state directly from onUpdate/onSelectionUpdate can land mid-render. Fixed per Tiptap's own performance guide by deferring the state update with queueMicrotask. Only surfaced because one E2E spec saved a document with blocks into a file another spec then opened -- the console gate caught it immediately.

set.body: Opening a note is clean (setContent uses emitUpdate:false), but switching WYSIWYG<->Markdown re-serializes and sets rawMarkdown to the serializer's output. When that differs from the bytes on disk only in formatting (table pipe padding, trailing newline), the note becomes dirty with no edit behind it and the 1.5s autosave rewrites the user's file. For a markdown editor that is a silent reformat of someone's document just for looking at it in another view. Fix: treat the post-load serialization as the dirty baseline, or only mark dirty on a real document change. Surfaced as an E2E flake: the autosave was still in flight when the page navigated, so the page-error gate saw an aborted POST /api/fs/write.
set.title: Switching view modes marks an unedited note dirty and autosaves

set.body: The Anthropic stream stops at max_tokens (8192) without telling anyone. set.resolution: Insert Table and /tab now escape the enclosing table (outermost, so an already-nested doc escapes fully) and append a sibling; the separating paragraph is what keeps two GFM tables from re-parsing as one. dispatchDocCommands resolves every locator against one snapshot of the document, folds commands touching the same table into a single rewrite, refuses genuinely overlapping edits by naming the pair, and applies right-to-left so offsets stay valid. Fixes the batch that failed with 'not found' or 'matches 2 places' when the model was right. Tool descriptions now state the contract.

set.body:
Two related problems, one symptom: an in-flight POST /api/fs/write cancelled when the page navigates, which the page-error gate correctly refuses to ignore.

1. Spurious dirty. Opening a note is clean (setContent uses emitUpdate:false), but switching WYSIWYG<->Markdown re-serializes and sets rawMarkdown to the serializer's output. Where that differs from the bytes on disk only in formatting (table pipe padding, trailing newline), the note goes dirty with no edit behind it and the 1.5s autosave rewrites the user's file -- a silent reformat just for looking at the note in another view. Fix: treat the post-load serialization as the dirty baseline, or mark dirty only on a real document change.

2. Nothing waits for autosave before teardown. Even on a legitimately edited note, the debounced save can still be in flight when a spec navigates or finishes. Measured on main before any of this work: e2e/persistence.spec.ts 'a new note can be edited, saved, and reloaded' fails roughly 1 run in 8 this way, and e2e/tables.spec.ts hit the same abort until its spec was made to settle the save explicitly. Worth a shared fixture helper that waits for quiescence rather than each spec remembering.

Note the redundant-write half is already fixed: handleSave now skips when a write is in flight or the content is unchanged, so autosave and an explicit Save no longer both put the same bytes on the wire.
set.title: Autosave races page teardown, so a write aborts and the E2E gate trips

set.body: Markdown and Split currently show raw source as unstyled mono text. Color headings, emphasis, inline and fenced code, links, and list markers in the Markdown source editor and the Split preview so the source is readable the way a markdown editor should be. Keep the control a labeled textarea (aria-label Markdown source) so Find, fill, and screen readers keep working — highlight sits behind it, not in a contenteditable. Use the lowlight highlighter already in the client bundle; do not add a second editor runtime. Light and dark tokens. No webfont CDN.
set.title: Syntax highlighting in Markdown and Split source

set.resolution: Hydration adopts Tiptap's serialized markdown as the clean baseline so view-mode switches and node-view reformats are not edits. Autosave only fires on a real byte change. E2E waitForSaveQuiescence waits for an in-flight Saving… (does not click Save — specs share a workspace).

Markdown mode is a labeled textarea with a lowlight highlight layer behind it; Split's right pane uses the same highlighter. No second editor runtime. Find, fill, and screen readers still hit the textarea.

Degrade-in-place: Dataset checks the workspace listing first (no 404). Missing demo files say 'Demo data is not in this workspace'; other missing sources name the path. Query catalog misses become 'Table X isn't registered'. DuckDB WASM init is a shared promise so welcome still loads Alice when the files exist.
